inputBoundary: One caller-supplied finite nonnegative duration in seconds for an already-reconstructed app-usage session.
outputBoundary: Classify the session as engage only when its supplied duration is strictly greater than sixty seconds; equality is not engage.
limitations: The source's separate greater-than-45-second inter-app break rule constructs sessions upstream; this binding does not reconstruct sessions from foreground/background events.

The paper says two duration-calculation methods were consistent but does not disclose either algorithm or which derived duration feeds this classification; the caller supplies the selected source-defined duration.
The source does not disclose timestamp ordering, missing-event handling, duration resolution, rounding, or tolerance; no sub-second measurement policy is inferred.
The adjacent at-most-15-second micro and 16-to-60-second review categories remain separate canonical settings and are not claimed by this one-atom fixture.
Negative, missing, or nonfinite duration fails closed instead of being converted into a zero-duration session.
